title: Bajersk Kräm med Jordgubbssaft (Bavarian Cream with Strawberry Juice)
description: Prepared with strawberry, cream, and gelatin.
steps: Rinse the gelatin in cold water, cut it into pieces and dissolve it in 1/2 dcl. boiling water together with the sugar, then add the strawberry juice.
When the mixture is completely cold and begins to set, fold in the cream whipped to stiff peaks.
Rinse a nice tin mold with cold water and sprinkle with caster sugar, pour in the mixture, and let the mold stand on ice for 3-4 hours.

When the pudding is to be served, loosen it around the edge with a pointed knife, turn it out onto a flat glass dish with cake paper and garnish with preserved strawberries, sponge cakes or macaroons.
Instead of strawberry juice, raspberry, gooseberry or cherry juice may be used.

title: Baked Whitefish (Ugnstekt sik)
description: Prepared with onion, rusks, and wine.
steps: If desired, add pepper and some dill sprigs.
Arrange the salmon pieces with the meat sides toward each other in such a way that the thick side of the fish is placed against the thin side.
Place it thereafter in light press between two cutting boards overnight and the fish is thereafter ready.
Cut into slices 1/2 cm thick, arrange them beautifully on a platter, garnish with fish skin halved on the stove or fried, and fresh dill sprigs.
Serve with cooking oil, vinegar, powdered sugar, French mustard, salt and pepper.
Cured fish can be cut into thin slices and seared in an almost dry frying pan. Serve as above.

title: Bakelser av smördeg (Butter Dough Pastries)
description: A pastry dish made with butter, flour, and water.

ingredients.name: 250 gr. fine butter (equal weight to the dough)
ingredients.sourceText: 250 gr. fine butter (equal weight to the dough)

steps: Prepare the butter dough as in recipe no. 33.
After the last resting, roll out to 1 cm. thickness and cut with a pastry wheel into round or square cakes.

Place a little applesauce in the center of the cakes, brush the round ones around the edge with a little water, then fold in half so the cake becomes a half-moon shape, press the edges together and lightly flute with a pastry wheel if desired.
For the square cakes, make an incision from each corner with the wheel and fold every other of the eight flaps over the applesauce and press together.
Bake the pastries in a warm oven.
This recipe makes approximately 12 butter pastries.

title: Balsk Ostronpudding (Baltic Oyster Pudding)
description: A pudding made with herring, skim milk, and rusks.

ingredients.name: butter (10 gr.) for the mold
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 tablespoon butter (10 gr.) for the mold

ingredients.name: crushed rusks for the mold
ingredients.sourceText: 2 tablespoons crushed rusks for the mold

steps: Rinse the herring milt well and let it soak in the skim milk for about 2 hours.
Wrap it in a fish towel, chop it finely and mix it with the finely crushed rusks, cream milk, clarified butter, well-whipped eggs and spices.
Pour the mixture into a buttered and breadcrumb-lined baking form and bake in the oven until it has taken on a beautiful golden-brown color, about 45 minutes.
Serve with clarified butter as a breakfast dish.

title: Banankompott (Banana Compote)
description: Prepared with vanilla bean, bananas, and sugar.
steps: Cook the sugar and water with the vanilla in an enameled iron pot until a clear, thin syrup forms.

Peel the bananas, cut into halves if desired, place in the sugar syrup, cover with a lid, and let the bananas rest in the syrup, which should be kept at 90°, until they are clear and soft, but do not allow them to boil.
Transfer to a compote bowl, reduce the syrup if desired, and pour over.
Serve with biscuits or sliced almonds.

title: Basic Recipe for Various Glace Bombs (Grundrecept till olika slags glacebomber)
description: Prepared with sugar syrup, egg yolks, and cream.

ingredients.name: 3 dcl. thick sugar syrup (3 hg. granulated sugar, 1 1/2 dcl. water)
ingredients.sourceText: 3 dcl. thick sugar syrup (3 hg. granulated sugar, 1 1/2 dcl. water)

steps: Cook the sugar syrup first, preferably the day before use
Chop the sugar into small pieces and place in an enameled iron pot, add water, and when the sugar is melted, cook it to a clear, syrupy consistency that should thread between the fingers when tested
Measure the sugar syrup and let it cool
Add the egg yolks one at a time while whisking, then let the cream simmer over heat with vigorous whisking
Pour the cream and whisk over ice until completely cold
Mix with the heavy cream, beaten to stiff peaks
The bomb cream can be flavored with vanilla, lemon, apricot, pineapple, kirsch, anisette, wild strawberries or strawberries, finely crushed nougat, finely chopped pistachios, cherry compote, etc.
Fill the cream into a bomb mold and freeze directly in it for 4-5 hours
Alternatively, the mold should preferably be lined inside with a thin layer of some kind of pre-frozen glace, filled with bomb cream, and frozen for 4-5 hours

title: Beignet-sufflé (20 pieces)
description: Prepared with wheat flour, butter, and milk.
steps: Bring butter and milk to a boil together, carefully stir in the flour, and let the batter cook until it leaves the sides of the pan, then remove from heat.
Add the egg yolks immediately one at a time, and when the batter is cold, carefully fold in the egg whites beaten to stiff peaks.
Form small balls of the batter with teaspoons and cook them in hot deep fat.
When the pastries have turned a beautiful light brown color, place them on gray paper to drain and sprinkle with fine sugar.
Serve warm or cold with jam.

title: Beignet-sufflé (Beignet Soufflé)
description: Prepared with milk, butter, and salt.
steps: Bring butter, milk, and spices to a boil, add the flour with vigorous whisking, and let the batter cook until it releases from the pan and has a golden color.
Remove the pan from heat, work in the eggs, one at a time, and stir the mixture 5 minutes.

Shape the mixture with two teaspoons, dipped in the cooking oil, into round balls the size of a walnut, which are poached a nice light golden color in moderately hot oil and placed on absorbent paper to drain, then sprinkled with sugar.
Serve very hot, placed on parchment paper, with chocolate sauce, jam, or compote.

title: Bergensisk fiskstuvning (Bergen Fish Braising)
description: Prepared with fish, crayfish, and wheat flour.
steps: Lay the crayfish tails in milk the evening before they are to be used.
Clean the fish and cut into large dice.
Lay it on the serving platter alternating with the crayfish tails, and place the platter over a pot of boiling water to heat through.
Melt the butter and flour together, add milk and fish broth little by little, and let the sauce boil for 10 minutes.
Season with salt and lemon juice and finish with the egg yolks.
Pour the sauce over the fish and serve at once.

title: Berlinerbröd (Berlin Bread)
description: A bread preparation made with sweet almonds, butter, and sugar.
steps: Dry the almonds in a cloth and chop fairly coarsely.

Place the dough with 2 spoons on a well buttered baking sheet in approximately 2 1/2 cm. wide strips, which are baked a nice golden brown in a not too hot oven.

title: Berlinermunkar (Berlin Doughnuts)
description: Prepared with juice, yeast, and wheat flour.

ingredients.name: apple sauce or currant jelly for filling
ingredients.sourceText: apple sauce or currant jelly for filling

steps: Warm the milk and blend it with the clarified butter, the beaten eggs, the sugar, the lemon peel and juice, and the yeast dissolved in a little warm milk.
Work in the flour, beat the dough smooth and glossy, and let it rise about 1 hour.
Work the dough and roll it out finger-thick, and cut small round cakes with a glass.
Place a little currant jelly or apple sauce in the middle of the cake and another cake on top; brush the edges with egg white and press them well together.
Let the doughnuts rise 1 hour.
Cook them in hot oil, place them on grey paper to drain, and roll in sugar.
Serve warm.

title: Biff av helgeflundra (Halibut Steak)
description: Prepared with halibut, white pepper, and vinegar.
steps: Free the halibut from skin and bones, and cook broth on these.
Cut the fish into 3 cm thick slices, which are lightly pounded and placed on a serving dish.
Sprinkle the slices with salt, pepper and, if desired, a little finely chopped onion.
Pour over enough vinegar so that it is level with the fish.
After two hours, remove the slices and dry well with a cloth.
Brown them in the butter and place on a warm dish.
Stir the flour in the pan, dilute with the fish broth, add soy and mustard, and let the sauce come to a good boil, taste it and pour it over the fish.
Place it on the serving dish and garnish with parsley and small butter pastry squares.

title: Biff av Kalvlever (Calf Liver Steaks)
description: Prepared with calf liver, white pepper, and onion.
steps: Let the liver soak in cold water for about 1 hour, dry with a meat cloth and remove the membrane.
Cut into slices 1 cm thick, sprinkle with salt and pepper and dredge in flour.
Brown the butter, add the steaks and fry until nicely brown on both sides, then place on a warm plate.
Peel the onion, cut into fine dice, brown in butter, which is then fried with flour for 2 minutes.
Pour in the broth and let the sauce simmer for 5 minutes, then season with soy sauce and spices.
Pour the sauce over the steaks, which can be garnished with fried, salted bacon slices.
Serve with potatoes as a breakfast dish.

title: Biff av ren (Reindeer Steak)
description: Prepared with skim milk or liquid, white pepper, and broth.

ingredients.name: skim milk or drinking liquid
ingredients.sourceText: 1 liter skim milk or drinking liquid

steps: If the meat is frozen, let it thaw in milk or drinking liquid. Dry it well with a cloth, trim and cut into 12 slices, which are lightly beaten, wrapped in a cloth, sprinkled with spices, brushed with 1 msk melted butter and left to lie on top of each other for 1 hour.
Heat a frying pan, brown the butter in it, place the steaks in and fry about 3 minutes on each side.
Arrange on a warm platter, whisk the pan with the broth and keep the sauce on the platter.

Place a slice of maitre-d'hôtel butter (see no. 406) on each steak; garnish the dish with parsley and serve with boiled or fried potatoes. The steaks can also be garnished with fried Portuguese onion, in which case the maitre-d'hôtel butter is omitted and the frying pan is whisked with 2 dcl thick cream, then the sauce is poured over the steaks.

title: Biffpaj (Beef Pie)
description: A pastry dish made with beef steak or tenderloin, smoked ham, and veal kidneys.

ingredients.name: Butter dough: 125 g butter, 125 g flour, 3-4 tbsp water
ingredients.sourceText: Butter dough: 125 g butter, 125 g flour, 3-4 tbsp water

steps: The butter dough is prepared as simple butter dough.
The onion is blanched for 10 minutes. The veal kidneys are blanched and cut into thin slices; likewise the onion and ham.
From the beef steak, thin, well-beaten steaks are prepared, which are turned in a mixture of salt, white pepper and flour.
In a fireproof form of clay or porcelain, first a layer of onion is placed, over it a layer of beef slices, then a layer of ham and veal kidney, and so it continues until the form is filled.
The water is added, and 3/4 of the butter dough is placed over the pie as a lid. With a larding needle, holes are made in a few places in the dough so that gases formed during baking can escape.

The pie is brushed with egg white. The remaining butter dough is rolled out thin and cut into narrow strips. With it the pie is lined in a grid pattern, or it is garnished with small leaves cut from the butter dough. Finally, the pie's edges are also covered with a strip of butter dough.
It is brushed over with beaten egg or water and baked in a hot oven for approximately 1½ hours.

title: Biffpaj (Beef Pie)
description: A pastry dish made with beef, white pepper, and onions or onion.
steps: If a beef cooker is lacking, the beef can be arranged in a fireproof so-called pie form with a pastry lid, and is then called beef pie.
Prepare as in recipe 485, with or without potatoes. In the latter case, serve the potatoes with the pie. It can also be supplemented with cooked ham or calf kidney, according to taste.
Whisk the broth with the flour and add last.
For the pie dough, mix all ingredients on the work bench and roll out the dough to 1 cm. thickness.
Cut a lid for the form, brush the edges of the form with water, and press the dough lid firmly.
With a fork or larding needle, make 4-6 holes in the dough so that the gases formed during baking may escape.
Brush the pie with egg white and garnish with the rest of the dough, cut into beautiful figures, which are also brushed with egg white.
Bake in ordinary oven heat for approximately 1 1/2 hours. Serve from the form.
The pie can also be baked in a tinned copper form or sheet form, but then double the amount of dough is needed, and the form is lined with it. Otherwise prepare as above.

title: Biffstek (Beef Steak)
description: Prepared with beef, white pepper, and bouillon.

ingredients.name: beef sirloin, ox loin, boneless inner loin or fillet
ingredients.sourceText: 1 kg beef sirloin, ox loin, boneless inner loin or fillet

ingredients.name: 3–4 red onions or 1 large Portuguese onion
ingredients.sourceText: 3–4 red onions or 1 large Portuguese onion

steps: The meat, which should have hung until properly tender, is dried with a cloth wrung out in hot water, cut across the muscle fibers in approximately 1.5 cm thick slices, which are beaten with a moist meat mallet or meat tenderizer until thin, but must not be beaten to pieces. If fillet is used, the meat slices are only lightly tapped with a knife.
The steaks are sprinkled with the seasonings.
The onion is peeled, cut into slices and fried first in part of the butter and placed in the center of a warm serving dish.
The frying pan is rinsed out with hot water and heated over a brisk flame; enough butter is added so that it covers the bottom of the pan when melted.
When the butter is brown, the steaks are added and fried approximately 2 minutes on each side, or until they are nicely brown.
They are arranged in a ring around the onion and covered either with browned butter or the frying pan is rinsed out with the bouillon and the sauce is poured over the steaks.
Served with fried potatoes, sprinkled with finely chopped parsley.
If the steaks are desired rare inside, they should be somewhat thicker and fried only 1 minute on each side.

title: Biffstek med falsk sköldpaddsås (Steak with False Turtle Sauce)
description: A sauce made with pork, white pepper, and bacon.

ingredients.name: 8 dcl. strong veal broth (made from the bones)
ingredients.sourceText: 8 dcl. strong veal broth (made from the bones)

steps: For the sauce, brown the butter with the bacon, cut into cubes, and the cleaned and chopped vegetables.
When the vegetables are well browned, add the broth, tomato purée and soy, then let everything cook for 1 1/2 hours.
Dry the pork loin with a cloth, wring out in hot water, and cut into slices, which are pounded on both sides and sprinkled with salt and pepper.
Let the steaks rest while the sauce finishes cooking.
Strain and skim the broth. Fry the butter and flour for 2 minutes, add the broth gradually, and let the sauce cook under stirring for 5 minutes.
Season with the wine, cognac and cayenne.
Fry the steaks quickly in butter, place on a warm serving dish and pour the sauce over.
Serve with potatoes or hard-boiled eggs as a breakfast dish.

title: Biskvipudding (Biscuit Pudding)
description: A biscuit made with biscuits, gelatin, and cream.
steps: Dry the biscuits in a warm oven and crush them, not too finely, in a mortar. Rinse the gelatin, cut it into pieces and dissolve it in the water. Whip the cream with 1 tbsp. of the sugar to stiff peaks, and gradually fold in the cooled gelatin, the remaining sugar, vanilla sugar and the crushed biscuits. Pour the mixture into a water-rinsed and sugar-sprinkled mold and let it set on ice for 2-3 hours. When the pudding is to be served, loosen it from the edge with a pointed knife and turn it out onto a flat glass plate with parchment paper. Garnish with fruit and jelly.

Press the remaining dough through a pastry bag in squares over the bottom.
Bake the cake in a not too hot oven until it is beautifully golden brown but must not be completely dry.
When the cake has cooled, fill the squares with cooked, pitted sour plums or yellow plums and jelly in various colors.

The bottom of the mold can advantageously be garnished with red wine gelée.

title: Blandad Frukt med Maräng (Mixed Fruit with Meringue)
description: Prepared with apricots, apples, and prunes.
steps: Rinse the apricots well and soak in water for about 1 hour
Cook a clear syrup from this water and sugar
Peel the apples, cut into 4 pieces, place directly in the syrup (to preserve color) and cook until clear
Remove with a slotted spoon, place the apricots in and let them cook until clear, then remove
Finally place the prunes in and let them cook soft
When the fruit is cold, arrange it in alternating layers, in pyramid form on a heat-resistant dish
Whip the egg whites until stiff peaks form and gently fold in the sugar
Pipe the meringue batter through a fluted piping bag over the fruit and place the dish in a mild oven heat
When the meringue has dried and turned a light yellow color, remove it and serve cold with whipped cream

title: Blandad Frukt med Maräng (Mixed Fruit with Meringue)
description: Prepared with prune, apricots, and apples.
steps: Rinse the dried fruit well in several lukewarm waters, let drain on cloth and layer alternately with caster sugar in a pot.
Add water and let the fruit stand for approximately 12 hours.
Pour off the water and cook it with the crushed sugar to a clear syrup, then let cool.
Wash, dry, peel, and cut the apples into 4-6 wedges, removing the cores.
Place them in the sugar syrup and cook until they are soft, but do not let them fall apart.
Remove with a slotted spoon and let cool, then cook the syrup until it is as thick as jelly.
On a silver dish, arrange the apples, plums, and apricots alternately, placing some of the reduced syrup between each layer.
Prepare the meringue as in the preceding recipe and pipe through a piping bag in beautiful streaks over the fruit.
Place in low oven heat.
When the meringue is half-dry and has a light yellow color, remove the arrangement and let cool.
Serve with whipped cream or vanilla sauce.

title: Blandad frukt med maräng (Mixed Fruit with Meringue)
description: Prepared with meringue, apricots, and apples.

ingredients.name: Meringue mass: 3 egg whites, 3-6 tablespoons powdered sugar
ingredients.sourceText: Meringue mass: 3 egg whites, 3-6 tablespoons powdered sugar

steps: Rinse the apricots well and soak them in water for about 1 hour.
From this water and the sugar, boil a clear syrup.
Peel the apples, cut them into 4 parts, place them directly in the syrup (to maintain their color) and cook until clear.
Remove them with a slotted spoon, place the apricots in and let them likewise cook until clear, then remove them.
Finally place the prunes in and let them cook until soft.
When the fruit is cold, arrange it alternately in a pyramid shape on a heat-resistant dish.
Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form, and carefully fold in the sugar.
Pipe the meringue mass through a fluted piping bag over the fruit, and place the dish in gentle oven heat.
When the meringue mass is dry and has taken on a light yellow color, remove it, and serve the dish cold with whipped cream.

title: Blandad färs av fågel (Mixed Poultry Forcemeat)
description: Prepared with chicken, game, and sauce.

ingredients.name: I. Chicken forcemeat: 1 hen, 100 gr. butter, 2 eggs, 1 part cream, twelve-öre wheat bread for panading, 2 parts boiling milk, salt, white pepper, 1.75 glas truffle at 1.50 kr. by weight against the forcemeat
ingredients.sourceText: I. Chicken forcemeat: 1 hen, 100 gr. butter, 2 eggs, 1 part cream, twelve-öre wheat bread for panading, 2 parts boiling milk, salt, white pepper, 1.75 glas truffle at 1.50 kr. by weight against the forcemeat

ingredients.name: II. Game forcemeat: 3 partridges, 100 gr. butter, 2 eggs, 1 part cream, twelve-öre wheat bread for panading, 2 parts boiling milk, salt, white pepper, 0.25 glas truffle at 1.50 kr. half the weight against the forcemeat
ingredients.sourceText: II. Game forcemeat: 3 partridges, 100 gr. butter, 2 eggs, 1 part cream, twelve-öre wheat bread for panading, 2 parts boiling milk, salt, white pepper, 0.25 glas truffle at 1.50 kr. half the weight against the forcemeat

ingredients.name: Sauce: 1 tbsp. butter, 2 tbsp. flour, game stock, 1 part thick cream, 0.5 glas truffle at 1.50 kr.
ingredients.sourceText: Sauce: 1 tbsp. butter, 2 tbsp. flour, game stock, 1 part thick cream, 0.5 glas truffle at 1.50 kr.

steps: Pluck the hen, clean it and rinse it well. Loosen the meat from the bones (cook stock on the carcass), cut it into cubes and pass three times through a meat grinder.
Prepare the panade as in the previous recipe and pass it through a sieve.
Pound the meat and butter well together in a stone mortar and pass through a fine sieve.
Gradually blend the whisked egg yolks, cream and seasonings into the forcemeat, which is worked for 1 hour. Then add the finely cut truffle and egg whites beaten until stiff.
If the forcemeat is too stiff, add a little cream, otherwise an egg yolk.
Prepare the game forcemeat in the same way.
Butter a fine pipe or à-la-daube mold and coat it with bread. In the mold, arrange alternating layers of the light chicken forcemeat.

Peel the onion and cut it into thin slices.
Brown the butter in a frying pan and fry the patties a beautiful brown in it, then lay them on a warm platter.
Whisk the pan with a little boiling water and pour the sauce over the patties.
Brown the onion in butter at the end and garnish the patties with it.

title: Blodpudding (Blood Pudding)
description: A pudding made with blood, broth, and syrup.
steps: Strain the blood through a fine sieve and whisk it well, then add the syrup and broth.
Whisk in the flour, add the finely chopped kidney fat and spices.
Peel and finely chop the onion, brown it in cream and stir it last into the mixture.
Fry a little of the mixture to taste if it is properly seasoned.

Butter a beautiful metal mold and dust it with crushed breadcrumbs, fill it two-thirds with the mixture and bind it over with buttered paper, then place it in boiling water and let it cook for 2-3 hours.
Test with a whisk to see if the pudding is done.

title: Blomkål med Äggstanning (Cauliflower with Egg Custard)
description: Prepared with cauliflower, wheat flour, and bread crumbs.

steps: Treat and cook the cauliflower heads as in recipe 709, let drain on a sieve, divide into florets, and place them in a buttered and bread-crumb-covered ovenproof mold.
For the egg custard, whisk the egg yolks with flour, salt, sugar, and milk, then fold in the egg whites whipped to stiff peaks.
Pour the egg custard over the cauliflower and sprinkle with parsley if desired.
Place the mold in a regular oven and let it stand until the custard is baked and has a nice color.
Serve with sausages, roasted meat, or as a course dish. In the latter case, sprinkle the custard with 1 tablespoon grated cheese instead of parsley before putting it in the oven.

title: Blåbärskräm (Bilberry Cream)
description: Prepared with bilberries, potato starch, and sugar.

ingredients.name: fresh or 1/2 liter bottled bilberries
ingredients.sourceText: 1 liter fresh or 1/2 liter bottled bilberries

steps: Clean the bilberries, rinse them in a sieve and let them drain.
Cook a thin, clear syrup from the sugar and water.
Add the bilberries and let them cook until they begin to fall apart.
Mix both types of flour with 1 dcl. cold water and slowly stir the mixture into the cream, which should not boil as it will become lumpy.
Let the cream cook for 5 minutes while stirring.
Pour into a compote dish rinsed with lukewarm water and sprinkle with sugar to prevent a skin from forming.
Serve with milk or cream.
If desired, the berries can be strained out and only the juice used. In this case, 1 tsp. good butter may advantageously be added, which prevents the cream from becoming stringy.
If bottled bilberries are used, they need only one boil in the sugar syrup.

title: Blåbärspaj (Blueberry Pie)
description: A pastry dish made with sweet almonds, egg yolk, and blueberries.

ingredients.name: butter (10 gr.) for the pan
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 tbsp. butter (10 gr.) for the pan

ingredients.name: crushed rusks for the pan
ingredients.sourceText: 2 tbsp. crushed rusks for the pan

steps: Sift the flour into a bowl; the butter, which should be firm, is divided into flakes in the flour and quickly worked in with the fingertips until the mixture is even and light yellow in color. Then add the sugar, the blanched and ground almonds, water and egg yolk quickly, and knead the dough a couple of times, roll into a ball, place immediately in a napkin and set in a cold place to rest 1 hour.
Clean the blueberries, rinse them, let them drain, sprinkle with sugar and mix well by shaking them.

Roll out three-quarters of the dough and line a buttered baking sheet or pan with it. Add the blueberries and fold the dough edge over. Roll out the remaining dough into a cover and cover the pie with it. Bake in good oven heat approximately 1 hour, or until the dough is thoroughly baked when tested with a whisk. Turn the pie out and serve warm or cold with whipped cream.

title: Boeuf à la Mode (Beef in Its Own Gravy)
description: A sauce made with lard, white pepper, and beef broth.
steps: The meat, which should have hung until properly tender, is prepared and larded with 2 hg of the lard (see page 232), rubbed with the remaining spices and tied so that it has a beautiful shape.

The butter is browned in a roasting pot, the meat is placed in it and browned on all sides until a beautiful brown crust is formed, then the remaining lard with the marrow is placed under the roast, the broth is added and the well-cracked and washed veal bones are placed in.

The broth is brought to a boil and well skimmed, after which the whole spices, the seared carrots and peeled onions, wine and cognac are added and the meat is allowed to stew slowly with the lid tightly closed, until tender, or about 3 hours, turning it a few times during cooking.

The roast is sliced, placed on a hot platter, moistened with a couple of tablespoons of sauce and garnished with the beautiful veal bones, the nicely cut carrots and onions as well as parsley or salad. Served with boiled potatoes, pickles or pressed cucumber and strained sauce (see no. 429).

title: Boeuf à la Mode (Beef in the Mode)
description: Prepared with beef, lard, and calf's foot.
steps: Wash the meat with a cloth dipped in hot water
Cut the lard into strips, roll in salt and pepper, and lard the meat in dense rows

Tie the meat with string (first dipped in boiling water) and place in a pot together with the blanched pork rind, blanched calf's foot, remaining salt, white peppercorns, cloves, wine, cognac, peeled onion, scraped carrots, and broth
Bring to a boil and skim well
Cover with a tightly fitting lid and let the meat simmer slowly for 3-4 hours
When tender, remove the meat and take off the string
Slice the meat and place on a warm plate, sprinkle with a little salt, and garnish with sliced carrots and fried onions, serve with French potatoes
Strain the broth, skim well, taste, and serve with the meat
The sauce can be finished according to general sauce-making rules if desired

The butter is browned in a braising pot, the meat is placed in and browned on all sides until a nice brown crust is formed, then the rest of the lard with the marrow is placed under the meat, the stock is added and the well-cracked and washed veal knuckles are placed in.

The stock is brought to a boil and well skimmed, after which the whole spices, the browned carrots and the peeled onions, the wine and cognac are added and the meat is slowly braised with a tightly closed lid until tender, or approximately 3 hours, during which it is turned a few times.
The meat is sliced, placed on a warm dish, covered with a couple of tablespoons of sauce and garnished with the creamy veal knuckles, the beautifully sliced carrots and onions and parsley or salad.
Served with boiled potatoes, pickles or pressed cucumber and reduced sauce (see no. 429).

title: Boeuf à la Mode (Braised Beef)
description: Prepared with beef, lard, and calf's foot.
steps: Wash the meat with a cloth dipped in hot water
Cut the lard into strips, roll in salt and pepper, and lard the meat in tight rows

Tie the meat with twine (first dipped in boiling water) and place in a pot with the blanched pork rind, blanched calf's foot, remaining salt, white peppercorns, cloves, wine, cognac, peeled onion, scraped carrots, and broth
Bring to a boil and skim well
Cover tightly and let the meat simmer slowly for 3-4 hours
When tender, remove the meat and take off the twine
Slice the meat and arrange on a warm platter, sprinkle with a little salt, and garnish with sliced carrots and fried onions
Serve with French potatoes
Strain the broth, skim well, taste, and serve as gravy with the meat
If desired, the sauce can be thickened according to general sauce-making rules

title: Boiled Cold Salmon (Kokt, kall lax)
description: Prepared with salmon, broth, and vinegar.

ingredients.name: For white aspic: 1 liter fish broth
ingredients.sourceText: For white aspic: 1 liter fish broth

ingredients.name: For red aspic: 4 dcl fish broth
ingredients.sourceText: For red aspic: 4 dcl fish broth

ingredients.name: For garnish: mayonnaise, capers or truffle, beets, tomatoes, green salad, parsley, hard-boiled eggs
ingredients.sourceText: For garnish: mayonnaise, capers or truffle, beets, tomatoes, green salad, parsley, hard-boiled eggs

steps: Prepare the broth and clean the salmon as in the previous recipe.
If the salmon is to be served on two platters, split it lengthwise into two halves and carefully remove the bone.
Place both halves with the bone in the cold broth and cook as in recipe 327.
Let the salmon cool in the broth.
From the broth, prepare white and red aspic as in recipe 181.
Let a little of the white fish aspic set on the bottom of the platters where the salmon will be served.
Place the salmon on top.
Remove the skin in 3 cm wide strips running crosswise, leaving the skin in equally wide strips between.
Where the skin has been removed, spread mayonnaise mixed with a little white fish aspic and let set.
Garnish the mayonnaise with capers or truffle in beautiful figures, such as French fleurs-de-lis or royal crowns.
Garnish the remaining strips with white and red fish aspic, piped through a fine pastry bag, and small slices of beets or tomatoes.
Garnish the platter with green salad, parsley, hollowed-out tomatoes filled with vegetable salad, egg halves with fluted edges, and aspic.
Serve with mayonnaise or remoulade sauce.

title: Boiled Salted Ox Tongue (for 8–10 persons)
description: Prepared with ox tongue and water.
steps: The tongue, which should be lightly salted (see salting of beef), should lie for a couple of hours in chilled water, is placed in cold water, skimmed, and boils for 15 minutes at 100°. The broth is then cooled to 82°–83° and at this temperature the tongue lies for 3½ hours, or until the skin can easily be drawn off. It is then placed in a stone pot with a flat bottom, the broth is poured over and the tongue is allowed to cool in it — it becomes juicier if allowed to cool in the broth. If it is to be served warm, it should be warmed in the broth after the skin has been removed. If the tongue is to be served with mixed meat dishes, it is sliced as in no. 493. For cold sliced tongue, thinner slices are cut, and then it is most economical to begin slicing from the tip of the tongue. If the tongue is heavily salted, it should lie in water for about 12 hours.

title: Boiled Warm Salmon (Kokt, varm lax)
description: Prepared with salmon, broth, and vinegar.
steps: In a pot, add the water and vinegar. Add the salt, the scraped carrot cut into small pieces, the peeled onion, bay leaf, and parsley, and let the broth boil for 1 hour.
Ten minutes before it is done, add the peppercorns.
Strain the broth through a fine sieve, taste, and let cool.
Scale the salmon, clean without cutting too much, and wash well with a cloth dipped in cold water, then dry.

The salmon can be boiled whole, split lengthwise into two halves (the bone is removed but cooked with the fish), or cut into 3–4 cm thick slices; cook in the broth according to the instructions in recipe 327.
Serve with hollandaise, mousseline, crayfish, or shrimp sauce and small boiled potatoes.
Leftover boiled salmon can be used for mayonnaise (recipe 176), salad (recipe 177), or gratin (see sole gratin recipe 377).

title: Bomb med jordgubbar (Strawberry Bomb)
description: Prepared with cream, gelatin, and strawberry jam.
steps: The cream is whisked to stiff peaks.
Half of it is mixed with the vanilla sugar and frozen in an ice machine.
The strawberries are strained and mixed with the remaining cream, and the mixture is colored with a little carmine.
The gelatin is rinsed with cold water, dissolved in a little hot water, and stirred in.
A bomb mold is lined with the frozen cream, filled with the pink mixture, and set to freeze further in ice and salt.
Between the cream and the lid, a layer of buttered paper is placed to prevent water or salt from entering.

title: Borgö-bakelser (Borgö Pastries)
description: A pastry dish made with melted butter, lemon or sweet almonds, and potato flour.

ingredients.name: zest of 1/2 lemon or 15 sweet almonds
ingredients.sourceText: zest of 1/2 lemon or 15 sweet almonds

ingredients.name: 20 gr. melted butter for the molds
ingredients.sourceText: 20 gr. melted butter for the molds

steps: Grease small decorative pastry molds with melted butter and let it set, then sprinkle with crushed, sifted rusks.
Let the butter cool and stir until white and creamy, then add the sugar, egg yolks one at a time, the finely grated lemon zest or the blanched and ground almonds, and the potato flour.
Finally fold in the egg whites, beaten to stiff peaks.
Fill the molds three-quarters full with batter, place on a baking sheet, and bake in a not-too-hot oven until dry when tested with a skewer.
Turn out when most of the heat has dissipated, and serve with cream or fruit or with coffee or tea.

title: Bouchéer med kräftstuvning (Crayfish Pastry Puffs)
description: A pastry dish made with crayfish, egg white, and cream.
steps: Prepare the puff pastry as in no. 33, roll out to 3/4 cm. thickness, and cut small round cakes with a drinking glass.
Place half of these on a baking sheet; hollow out the centers of the other half with a wine glass so they become rings.
Brush the cakes with egg white, then place the rings on top.
Lay the bouchées on a baking sheet along with the small lids and brush both parts on top with egg white, which must not run down the sides as it prevents the puff pastry from rising.
Bake until light brown in a hot oven.
Carefully remove the puff pastry that has risen in the center of the bouchées during baking, making room for the filling.
Place the crayfish tails in milk several hours before use.
Strain them well in a colander.
Fry the butter and flour for 2 minutes, add the cream and let the sauce boil for 5 minutes, then add the crayfish tails and bring the stew to a boil and taste it.
If desired, add a whisked egg yolk and let the stew simmer.
Fill the bouchées while warm with the stew and place the lids on if desired.
Arrange the bouchées on pastry paper or on a broken napkin and serve as a middle course.

ingredients.name: cooked, deboned and finely cut fish

steps: Prepare the butter dough as ordinary butter dough. When it is ready, roll it out to 1 cm. thickness, and with a measure cut out small round cakes. With a knife cut small lids in these, but not deeper than 1/2 cm. (half the cake's thickness).
Brush the ring outside the lid with egg white, and to this fasten a strip of dough, cut with points. Bake the bouchées thereafter in a very hot oven.
Lift off the already cut lid, and fill the bouchées with fish stewing, whereafter the lid is laid on again.
The bouchées should be served very hot.

title: Braised Calf Brain (Stuvad kalvhjärna)
description: Prepared with cream, white pepper, and bread.
steps: Let the calf brain soak in water, changing it often so all blood is removed.
Blanch it as in recipe no. 47, for 45 minutes and place on a sieve.
When it is cold, remove all membranes and chop the brain with a knife on a cutting board.
Fry the butter in a saucepan, add the brain and fry well.
Add the cream and seasonings and let the stew come to a good boil.
Place on warm toast and garnish with small croutons (fried bread slices).
Serve to the smörgåsbord (open sandwich table).

title: Braxen med vin (Bream with Wine)
description: Prepared with bream, red wine, and broth.
steps: Scale and clean the fish (see page 171); the head may remain but must be freed from gills.
Rub it with salt and let it rest for 1 hour, then dry it again.
Brown the butter lightly and fry it with the flour for 2 minutes; add the wine and as much broth as needed to make the sauce properly thin.
Place the fish in a small fish kettle without a sieve together with the roe or milk; pour the sauce over it and it should stand level with the fish.

title: Briocher (Brioche Buns)
description: A bread preparation made with wheat flour, yeast, and milk.
steps: Sift the flour. Crumble the yeast into one third of the flour, then add the milk and work the dough, which should be loose, quickly and roll it into a ball on the work surface, making a cross on top.
Place the dough in a covered bowl and let it rise in a warm place for about 1 hour.
Work in the salt, sugar, cardamom pods if desired, and the eggs one at a time. Between each egg addition, work the dough for 5 minutes and add more flour so the dough becomes appropriately firm.
Roll out the dough and work in the butter as described in the previous recipe, then place it in a bowl, cover it, and let it stand in a moderately warm room for 6-8 hours.
After 3 hours, stop the rising by placing the dough on a floured work surface and slapping it with your hand. Return it to the bowl and let it rise for another 4-5 hours.

Place the dough in brioche molds, brush with egg, let it rise, and bake in a warm oven. Alternatively, it can be shaped into small round buns with a small indentation in the middle, filled with a small ball the size of a small nut. Treat the same as above.
Serve with coffee and tea.

title: Brudar med slöja (Brides with Veil)
description: Prepared with prunes, apricots, and apples.
steps: Rinse the fruit and let it soak in the water for about 1 hour.

Place the fruit and bread on a platter in layers so that they form a pyramid.
Whip the cream to stiff peaks, place it in a paper cone and pipe out as veils over the pyramid.
Serve with whipped cream.

title: Brun Sås (Brown Sauce / Spanish Sauce)
description: A sauce made with shallot, carrot, and smoked ham.

ingredients.name: 6 dcl. good meat stock from the roast
ingredients.sourceText: 6 dcl. good meat stock from the roast

steps: Peel and chop the onions and carrot into pieces, clean the parsley stems, rinse them, wring them in a cloth, and dice the ham. Brown everything lightly in 1 tbsp of butter.

Add the previously prepared meat stock and white wine and let simmer slowly with a lid for approximately 2 hours, then strain the liquid through a fine sieve, skim, and measure it—it should yield 8 dcl.

Fry the remaining butter with the flour for 2 minutes, gradually add the meat stock cooked with vegetables and the skimmed meat stock from the roast, then season with spices and Madeira and let cook while stirring for 15 minutes.
Season with more Madeira if desired. When using this sauce for game, omit the wine and season the sauce with 1–2 tbsp black or red currant jelly.

title: Brylé Pudding (Burnt Sugar Pudding)
description: A pudding made with sugar, egg yolks, and cream.

ingredients.name: 3 deciliters sugar for the mold (255 g)
ingredients.sourceText: 3 deciliters sugar for the mold (255 g)

steps: Brylé pudding is best if it is prepared the day before it is to be served.
Cook the sugar with the water until it is dry, then stir it until it becomes liquid again and has a nice light brown color.
Pour some of the sugar mixture into a pie mold, which is turned around so that the mixture covers both the bottom and the sides.
The remaining sugar mixture is diluted with water and served as sauce with the pudding.
Stir the egg yolks with the sugar for 20 minutes.

Heat the cream milk (2 deciliters cream, 3 deciliters milk) with the vanilla pod for about 5 minutes and add to the stirred egg yolks with vigorous beating; continue beating until the cream is cold, then remove the vanilla pod and fold in the egg whites beaten to stiff peaks.
Pour the cream into the coated mold, and let the pudding boil in a water bath in ordinary oven heat for about 1 1/2 hours.
Let it stand in the mold until the next day, or until it is completely cold. Turn it out and serve with the remaining brylé sauce.

title: Brylékräm (Brulée Cream)
description: Prepared with cream, vanilla bean, and gelatin.
steps: Melt the sugar in a slightly warm frying pan buttered with {{source-5}}; when it has a light brown color, add 1 deciliter of the water, and pour the sugar syrup into a saucepan.
Add the vanilla and let it boil, stirring over gentle heat for about 5 minutes, after which it is removed.
Rinse the gelatin, cut it into pieces, dissolve it in the rest of the water and pour it into the sugar syrup, which is then allowed to cool.
Whip the cream to stiff peaks and fold it gently into the sugar syrup.
Pour the cream into a water-rinsed and sugar-dusted mold and let it set on ice.
When the cream is to be served, loosen it from the edge with a pointed knife and turn it out onto a cake dish with cake paper.
Garnish with biscuits.

title: Brynt salt fårbringa (Browned Salted Lamb Breast)
description: Prepared with lamb, breadcrumbs, and water.
steps: If the lamb breast is too salty to boil directly, soak it the day before.

title: Brynt Vitkål (Browned Cabbage)
description: Prepared with cabbage, soy sauce, and broth.

ingredients.name: water, 1 tablespoon salt (15 gr.) for blanching
ingredients.sourceText: 3 liters water, 1 tablespoon salt (15 gr.) for blanching

steps: Remove the outer green leaves from the cabbage head, loosen the remaining leaves from the core and remove the thickest part of the main rib
Blanch the cabbage (place in boiling salted water and let cook 8-10 minutes without a lid), remove with a slotted spoon, let drain on cloth and cut into cubes or strips
Brown the butter and sugar in a pot, add the cabbage, pour the soy sauce over and brown with frequent stirring until it gets a nice color
Add the broth and let the cabbage cook slowly with a lid until completely tender, or about 3 hours
Season with salt and more sugar if desired
Serve with boiled or roasted pork and boiled sausage

title: Brynta Jordärtskockor (Browned Jerusalem Artichokes)
description: Prepared with jerusalem artichokes, water, and salt.
steps: Rinse the Jerusalem artichokes, brush them thoroughly clean, scrape them and place them gradually in vinegar-diluted water to prevent them from darkening.
Rinse them again, place them in boiling salted water and let them cook soft, which is tested with a whisk, drain in a colander and let them cool on a cloth.
Shape them afterwards like large olives with a knife or smooth vegetable knife and fry a beautiful light brown in the butter.
Serve as garnish around fried meat or together with other vegetables.

title: Brynta kålrötter (Browned Rutabaga)
description: Prepared with beef broth, white pepper, and water.
steps: The rutabagas are peeled (see page 338), cut into fairly large cubes or oblong squares, which are blanched 3-4 minutes with the lid open.
They are drained in a colander and allowed to drip dry on a cloth.
The butter is browned in an iron saucepan, the roots are added, sprinkled with sugar and salt and browned, while they are stirred often, until they acquire a nice color.
Then the broth is added and the roots are allowed to simmer slowly until they are completely soft, or about 1 1/2 hours.
They are seasoned with a little pepper, if desired, and are served with salted meat.

Drain them in a colander and let them dry on a cloth.
Brown the butter in an iron saucepan, add the rutabagas, sprinkle with sugar and salt and brown them, stirring often, until they get a nice color.
Then add the broth and let the rutabagas simmer slowly until they are completely tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Season with a little pepper if desired and serve with salt meat.

title: Brödpanad till Färs (Bread Panade for Forcemeat)
description: A bread preparation made with bread, salt, and milk.
steps: Remove the crusts from the wheat bread, weigh it and place it in a saucepan together with the salt.
Pour the boiling milk over it and when the bread has absorbed all the milk, place the saucepan over the heat and stir the panade with a wooden spoon or spatula until it is thick and smooth.
Pour the panade onto a buttered dish and brush a little butter over the top so that it does not dry while it cools.

title: Button Mushrooms as Garnish (Champinjoner till garnityr)
description: Prepared with mushrooms, juice, and water.
steps: The button mushrooms are cleaned as soon as they are picked: the gills are removed gently, the outer skin is not removed from tender mushrooms, the stems are cut level with the caps, then the mushroom is quickly rinsed and dried on a cloth.
The caps are scored beautifully with a pointed knife, immediately placed in boiling water, mixed with salt, butter and lemon juice and allowed to boil 5–10 min.
Remove with a slotted spoon and use as garnish around finer dishes.
The mushrooms can be kept 2–3 days in a cold place if they are covered with butter-brushed, so-called butter paper.

The broth is used for sauces and stews. Small preserved French button mushrooms can be scored in a similar way, placed in their broth, mixed with 1 tbsp. butter, boiled about 2 min. and used as before.

title: Béarnaise Sauce (Béarnaisesås)
description: Prepared with shallot, white pepper, and vinegar.

ingredients.name: good meat stock or fish bouillon
ingredients.sourceText: 3 tablespoons good meat stock or fish bouillon

steps: Mix the shallot, pepper, salt and vinegar in the sauce pan and reduce by boiling until 1/3 remains.
Move the pan to the side, add the whisked egg yolks and let the sauce simmer under vigorous whisking.
Add the melted, slightly cooled butter gradually.
Strain the sauce through a fine cloth, season with cayenne and finish with the chopped tarragon and, if desired, the meat stock or fish bouillon.
Heat in a water bath until lukewarm and serve at once. If overheated, it will break.
